behavior: Highly active insectivore that flits through foliage, gleans prey, and darts after insects in flight. Frequently flicks and fans its wings and tail to flush prey; migrates mostly at night and defends territories.
field_marks: Small, slim warbler with a broad, flat black bill and dark eye
Adult male mostly black with vivid orange patches on the sides, wings, and tail
Female and immature male gray and olive-brown with yellow to yellow-orange patches
Pale white to gray belly contrasts with the darker upperparts
Fairly long dark tail with colored basal panels; legs and feet black
habitat: Moist, open deciduous and mixed woodland, especially second-growth forest with a dense shrubby layer; also thickets and streamside woods. During migration it uses varied wooded or shrubby habitats, while nonbreeding habitats include forest, scrub, and mangroves.
